scope: Byte-preserving encoder raw prediction/reconstruction output fusion plus EOB dequantization/active-row traversal fusion

environment.coordination: Root serialized each screen with other agents build/test/timing work paused; unrelated host activity not controlled.

source_reference.role: Separate prediction read and reconstruction write dataflow; Go original numeric contract independently preserved.

protocol.input: 120-frame 1280x720 60 fps I420 FourPeople at 3 Mbps and Johnny at 9 Mbps
protocol.warmups: One baseline/candidate pair per case; 4 retained rows
protocol.samples: 3 alternating AB/BA/AB pairs per case; 12 retained rows
protocol.control: First 8 FourPeople frames with keyint=1; candidate/baseline pair; constructor included; 2 retained rows
protocol.statistic: 100*(1-exp(mean(log(candidate/baseline)))) per paired case for process wall and child user+system CPU
protocol.predata: At least 0.5% paired-GM wall saving and 2/3 faster wall pairs in at least one affected case; the other case must not exceed 1% wall or CPU regression; every fixed hash exact; single key control descriptive
protocol.policy: No unchanged retry, excluded row, additive attribution, or native remeasurement

previous_output_only.result: Rejected: missed0.5% predata gate. Retained, no unchanged rerun.

tests.encoder: 0.426s passed: frozen original reconstruction/error/scratch oracle, numeric/alias output kernel, public zero-allocation gate
tests.quantize: 0.362s passed: independent int64 numeric + separate row scan oracle across EOBs, scans, bitdepth8/10/12, txScale0/1/2 and int16/quantizer boundaries; partial panic destination state

compiler_evidence.body: Scalar dequant arithmetic fully inline, row tracking uses AND/ADD/CMP/CSINC, no dynamic divide, no per-coefficient CALL or stack load/store. Only normal call is destination memclr once before loop.
compiler_evidence.frames: New flat helper48B vs generic64B. reconInterTXBResult224B vs output-V1 240B.
compiler_evidence.unchanged_output: Same output-fusion code as V1, preserving alias fallback and vector materialization.
compiler_evidence.early_exit_tradeoff: Before-data caveat: the old separate scan stopped as soon as activeRows reached coefficient height. V2 computes the row maximum for every EOB entry, including entries after that bound saturates; dense prefixes can add row-max instructions despite removing the separate scan. The smaller frame and removed clamp-bound reload may offset that cost, but only the fixed screen can support the integrated result. If slower, inspect actual EOB and first-full-height prefix lengths before a changed iteration; no unchanged retry.

protocol.cases: Same120-frame FourPeople3M and Johnny9M plus8-frame forced-key control; stats off, effort0, MaxThreads/GOMAXPROCS1,GOGC100, defaultPGO; all fixed old hashes asserted.

manifest.scope: New integrated implementation; no isolated row-bound speedup or additive gain claim. Original raw-copy scope~0.54% Johnny sample, row-scan~0.81%; sampled CPU not precise wall shares.

predata_guard.guard: At least one affected 120-frame case has >=0.5% paired-geomean process wall savings and >=2/3 faster wall pairs. Other case has no >1% wall or CPU regression. Every fixed emitted hash must match; retain all rows.
predata_guard.control: Single 8-frame forced-key pair described separately; constructor-affected.
predata_guard.restrictions: No unchanged retries, no additive claims; root owns sequential exclusive window.

integration.timing: No timing repeated after integration; attribution remains the frozen b9e260f4 pair.

subsequent_publication_integration.semantic_review: PR26 changes separate entropy/tile files. The writer consumes the same immutable eight-byte scan metadata via exported field names; EOB scan order, coefficient values and reconstruction inputs/interfaces are unchanged. No conflict with output or flat dequant-row fusion.
subsequent_publication_integration.validation: No gates or timing repeated. The prior focused/public-byte/reconstruction gate remains recorded above; root independently verified PR26 fixed encoder bytes.

limitations: V2 measures the integrated output+row-bound implementation; no isolated row-fusion speedup or additive claim.
ARM64 is the only native SIMD timing/codegen platform; amd64 SIMD retains original output copy+add.
New row collection visits all EOB entries whereas the old separate scan stopped at full height. Dense prefixes can add bound-update instructions.
The old copy leaf includes prediction scratch work; Johnny raw-output copy samples were20ms of3720ms (~0.54%), versus30ms for the entire copy leaf.
Profile scope is sampled CPU, not precise wall-time share or an exact upper bound.
The process helper hashes encoded bytes; the separate public fixture verifies reconstruction.
One keycontrol pair is descriptive and includes constructor work.
No whole-corpus native gap or equal-quality claim.
